title: A lump in the groin
objective: Assess the access site and the limb beyond it after catheterization -- hematoma, pulses, color, warmth, sensation -- and apply firm pressure above the puncture for bleeding
secondaryObjectives: Care before and after diagnostic and interventional cardiac or vascular catheterization, including sheaths and arterial closure devices

sources.cite: Progressive care nursing certification exam handbook and test plan: Cardiovascular (20% of the exam)
sources.note: Relayed from the PCCN course seed (backend/supabase/seed/tracks/pccn.ts), which read the handbook 2026-11-14, not re-read: Cardiovascular is 20% of the exam. Scope only.
The objective and secondary objectives are the course's own titles.

sources.cite: Kern MJ. Back to basics: femoral artery access and hemostasis. Cath Lab Digest 2013;21(10)
sources.note: Relayed from the PCCN case femoral-access-retroperitoneal-bleed, which read it 2026-11-14 through a summarizing fetch, not re-read: the needle enters the artery higher than the skin entry site, so manual compression goes over the artery about an inch cranial to the skin incision; firm pressure for 15-20 minutes, longer on antiplatelet drugs; pedal pulses checked every 2-3 minutes during compression; more than 500 mL can be lost before anyone notices.
Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model. Disease courses, effect sizes and local waits are authored and carry FLAG.

brief.situation: 13:15 on a progressive care unit. Mr. Bakshi, 70, came back an hour ago from a stent through the right femoral artery. The sheath was pulled in the lab. He is on two antiplatelet drugs and says his groin feels 'tight'.
handover: Post-procedure order: flat bed rest with the right leg straight for the set hours, access site and pedal pulse checks every 15 minutes, firm manual pressure above the puncture for any bleeding or expanding hematoma, and the interventional fellow called at once.
Pedal pulses were strong in the lab. Blood pressure 132/78 at 12:30.
The fellow is in the catheterization lab two floors down.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Assess and act as you think the patient needs. Each assessment takes the time on its button.
Partway through you are asked to write what you think is happening. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: Mr. Bakshi's groin swelling is growing. What is happening, and what do you do?

parts.label: What is happening
parts.criteria: An expanding, tense swelling after femoral access on two antiplatelet drugs is arterial bleeding at the puncture; a normal hemoglobin early doesn't exclude it; the limb beyond must be checked.
parts.modelAnswer: It's an expanding hematoma: the artery is bleeding at the puncture, made worse by his two antiplatelet drugs. The hemoglobin was normal an hour ago but that won't show it yet.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Firm manual pressure about an inch above the skin puncture over the artery; pedal pulses during; fellow now; keep flat; mark and time the edge; hand off.
parts.modelAnswer: Hold firm pressure just above the skin puncture where the artery is, check the pedal pulses while I do, call the fellow now, keep him flat, and mark the edge.

noProgress.rationale: A bleeding femoral access site still uncontrolled an hour on is harm here.

unsafe.headline: Up too soon
unsafe.body: After femoral access, bed rest with the leg straight protects the puncture, especially on antiplatelet drugs.

worsened.headline: Hemorrhagic shock
worsened.body: A thigh can hide a lot of blood. Check the site often and hold pressure in the right place.

wrongRoute.headline: Left an hour
wrongRoute.body: An expanding hematoma needs pressure and the fellow now.

target.headline: Controlled in time
target.body: You checked the site and pulses, marked the edge, held pressure above the puncture and called within minutes. That is the expert path.

recovered.headline: Controlled, with delays
recovered.body: Check how long the hematoma grew before pressure and the call.

time_up.headline: Still bleeding
time_up.body: Access-site bleeding is controlled within minutes.

scoring.modelReasoning: After femoral access on two antiplatelet drugs, the site and the leg beyond it are checked often: size, pulses, color, warmth and sensation. An expanding, tense swelling is arterial bleeding. Pressure goes about an inch above the skin puncture, where the needle entered the artery, with the pedal pulse checked during it; the fellow comes now and he stays flat.
